About the Role We are looking for an early-career Application Security Engineer to help application teams adopt practical security controls and complete consistent, risk-based reviews. You will support application discovery, evidence collection, secure development activities, security testing and remediation follow-through under the guidance of experienced AppSec colleagues. Key Duties and Responsibilities Support discovery of applications and APIs, gather ownership and technology information, and maintain classification data such as criticality, exposure and data sensitivity. Coordinate evidence requests, review existing security information for relevance and identify missing, stale or out-of-scope evidence for reviewer attention. Guide standard-risk applications through defined security review activities, track required actions and prepare concise evidence-based review summaries for senior approval. Execute repeatable application security review steps using approved playbooks and escalate complex design, testing or risk questions. Run and interpret SAST, SCA, secrets, IaC, container, DAST and API scans where applicable; confirm context with development teams before creating actionable findings. Perform focused manual checks of web applications and APIs, including authentication, access control, input handling, error handling and obvious workflow abuse, within an approved scope. Triage potential findings, collect reproduction evidence, apply the severity methodology and obtain senior review for material or ambiguous issues. Track remediation commitments, review evidence and retest straightforward fixes; reopen or escalate where the weakness remains exploitable. Provide developers with approved secure-coding guidance, examples and links to standards; capture recurring questions for broader enablement. Assist threat-modelling workshops by documenting assets, data flows, trust boundaries, threats, assumptions and agreed actions. Maintain assessment notes, evidence links, decisions, metrics and governance records so another reviewer can understand what was tested and why. Support tool trials, regression checks and false-positive analysis, providing structured feedback on usability and detection quality. Engage constructively with application owners, engineers and control partners; communicate blockers early and keep actions moving. Foundational understanding of web technologies, HTTP, APIs, authentication, authorisation and common application vulnerabilities. Ability to read code or configuration in at least one language or technology stack and reason about insecure patterns. Experience with at least two security testing or code-analysis capabilities, through employment, internships, labs or substantial projects. Comfort working with evidence, structured checklists, issue trackers and documented processes without becoming purely process-driven. Clear written communication, attention to detail and willingness to ask for review when risk or evidence is unclear. Ability to organise multiple actions, meet commitments and work collaboratively with developers. Fluent English, spoken and written. Additional Practical Experience Experience with Azure DevOps, Git, CI/CD or cloud-hosted applications. Evidence of practical learning through labs, code-review exercises, security testing projects or cloud fundamentals training. Familiarity with OWASP Top 10, OWASP API Security Top 10, ASVS or threat-modelling approaches. Experience in financial services, SaaS or another regulated environment. Scripting ability in Python, PowerShell or Bash. Candidate Expectations Be curious, methodical and honest about the limits of the evidence. Use playbooks consistently while developing the judgement to know when they are insufficient. Write findings that developers can reproduce and fix. Respect testing boundaries, confidentiality and change controls. Learn actively from reviews and contribute from the Hyderabad office as part of a collaborative team Disclaimer : Unsolicited CVs sent to Apex (Talent Acquisition Team or Hiring Managers) by recruitment agencies will not be accepted for this position. About the Role We are looking for an offensive security engineer to deliver authorised internal penetration tests of applications and APIs and to support broader red-team exercises. You will combine structured methodology with manual curiosity to find weaknesses that scanners and standard control checks miss. The role requires disciplined evidence, safe testing and clear reporting. You will work within approved rules of engagement and escalate immediately if test activity could affect service, data or users. Location: Hyderabad, India. This is an office-based position and is not available as a remote role. Key Duties and Responsibilities Execute internal web application and API penetration tests using approved methodologies, test plans and rules of engagement. Test authentication, session management, authorisation, input handling, data exposure, file processing, API object access and workflow controls. Develop misuse and abuse cases from business processes, user roles and trust assumptions; explore ways legitimate functionality could be manipulated. Use interception proxies, API clients, fuzzers, scanners and scripts to support—not replace—manual analysis. Inspect client-side code, API documentation, requests, responses and relevant source or configuration where access is approved. Document reproducible steps, requests and responses, affected roles, preconditions, impact and safe proof of exploitability. Remove false positives and duplicates, apply the severity methodology and seek peer review for high-risk or ambiguous findings. Prepare clear technical reports and concise summaries; explain findings to development teams without relying on jargon. Retest remediated findings and record whether the original attack path and relevant variants are closed. Support senior testers during objective-led red-team or purple-team exercises, including evidence capture and controlled validation. Create small scripts, test data and harnesses to improve repeatability; keep tooling approved, updated and securely stored. Share recurring vulnerabilities and root causes with AppSec engineers so guidance, threat models and pipeline controls can improve. Maintain accurate engagement status, evidence location, finding records and handover notes. Knowledge, Skills and Experience Typically 2-5 years in penetration testing, application security or security testing, with demonstrable hands-on web or API testing. Good understanding of HTTP, web architecture, REST APIs, cookies/tokens, authentication, authorisation and common vulnerability classes. Practical experience with an interception proxy and API-testing tools, plus basic scripting in Python, PowerShell, Bash or similar. Ability to distinguish a theoretical weakness from a reproducible, impactful security finding. Clear report writing with accurate evidence, remediation guidance and professional communication. Understanding of testing safety, confidentiality, approvals and responsible handling of credentials and sensitive data. Ability to receive peer review positively and improve testing based on feedback. Fluent English, spoken and written. Additional Practical Experience Evidence of practical offensive security development through hands-on labs, testing projects or structured training. Experience testing GraphQL, gRPC, mobile back ends, single-page applications or modern identity protocols. Exposure to Azure, Microsoft Entra ID, containers or CI/CD security. Secure code review or software development experience. Experience in financial services or another regulated environment. Candidate Expectations Stay within scope and use safe proofs; immediately report unexpected access or service impact. Test the business process, not only the endpoint or vulnerability checklist. Write with precision and avoid inflated severity or unsupported claims. Collaborate respectfully with the teams whose systems are being tested. Develop your tradecraft through deliberate practice and active participation from the Hyderabad office.
